Q: Arduino: reading output in python A:

What I’d like specifically is to have a real time processing of the data. I have an adafruit temperature sensor and I’d like to be able basically press a button and return a vector containing the temperature and python variable at the time. The main thing is that everything I’ve seen on the arduino website doesn’t seem to work for this method if I want to use the particular API adafruit uses, but I also might have missed something (kind of new to arduino stuff). Serial seems to output the entire dataset the arduino has been collecting, when I just want a little snapshot. Mb if I wasn’t clear, I didn’t explain it super well in the post.

Q: How to test a randomized input used to determine a final result on assertions? A:

A key assumption is that you accept the initial implementation as truth. Use the pseudo-Random approach to generate a resource-file that correlates sets of inputs to their expected outputs. Then modify the test to use that file to test each case individually in a parameterized test. This will allow you to identify which cases are failing when an update is made.

This approach can be useful when migrating from a legacy implementation that is accepted as canon to a new one where we want to be within some tolerance of the original. A large variety of input sets may also reveal hidden edge cases over time. However, each such case should lead to the creation of a unit test that targets that use case. In a sense, the bulk test is just used to identify where we should be creating unit tests.

Maintenance can be tricky. Ultimately, you need to regenerate the resource-file when the bulk test fails. However, you should not regenerate it without adding unit-test support to cover the cases that produced failures due to a change in expectations.

Q: Getting all tables / columns and their datatype firebird in one query A:

FIELD_TYPE and FIELD_SUB_TYPE is encoded by a number. Here is the translation to the type text:

https://www.firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/chunk/en/refdocs/fblangref25/fblangref-appx04-fields.html

FIELD_TYPE description text:

Data type code for the column:
7 - SMALLINT `8 - INTEGER `10 - FLOAT 12 - DATE 13 - TIME 14 - CHAR 16 - BIGINT 27 - DOUBLE PRECISION 35 - TIMESTAMP 37 - VARCHAR 261 - BLOB
Codes for DECIMAL and NUMERIC are the same as for the integer types used to store them

Q: How to send axios post request with date object in request body? A:

A couple of years too late but from the comments I would gather that OP wanted to take a date object and get an ISO8601 string out of it, it is possible using the .toISOString method.

The toISOString() method of Date instances returns a string representing this date in the date time string format, a simplified format based on ISO 8601, which is always 24 or 27 characters long (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ or ±YYYYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ, respectively). The timezone is always UTC, as denoted by the suffix Z.

For example:

new Date().toISOString()
//2026-07-07T14:39:08.148Z

Q: Hide a particular header and its corresponding column in vuetify datatable A:

Expanding on SimonDepelchin's answer:

The align property in the header specification of a given column, e.g.

{ text: 'some text', value: 'category', align: 'XXX' },

is converted into a class property of the given <td> element like this

<td class="text-XXX">{{item.category}}</td>

If XXX begins with a space, you can use this to give the td cell any class you like:

{ text: 'some text', value: 'category', align: ' d-none' },

becomes

<td class="text- d-none">{{item.category}}</td>

d-none is defined in vuetify.min.css as .d-none{display:none!important}. However, you do not need to load vuetify.min.css for this trick to work: just put .d-none{display:none!important} anywhere in your css definition.

Note, however, that when the table responsively changes to mobile view, the value of align is ignored, and thus the corresponding element is not hidden.

Q: Outlook web add-in starts with error when use displayInFrame:true A:

I had the same issue in an Excel add-in. The taskpane looked frozen until I cleared both errors. This only happened when a user of the add-in was logged-out. It turned out that we were not initializing the Office runtime in this state, which made Excel believe that the taskpane was broken.
